description: Create the architecture diagram as three consistent files that accurately reflect THIS project's real architecture (verified against infra/lib/digital-monster-stack.ts): docs/architecture.drawio (editable draw.io source using AWS icons), docs/architecture.svg (hand-authored vector matching the drawio), and docs/architecture.png (raster of the SVG for README embedding). Also add docs/aws-icons/ with the AWS icon assets the diagram references, matching the reference repo's pattern. All three diagram files MUST depict the same diagram.
steps: Create the docs/ directory and docs/aws-icons/ directory at the repo root.

Study the reference conventions cached at .tmp-ref/: architecture.drawio (draw.io XML using shape=mxgraph.aws4.resourceIcon; resIcon=mxgraph.aws4.cloudfront/.s3/etc inside a dashed 'AWS Cloud'/'AWS Account (us-east-1)' boundary) and architecture.svg (inlines official AWS architecture-icon <path> data with brand colors, white-on-color squid). Reuse what is reusable.

Populate docs/aws-icons/ with the AWS icon .svg assets the diagram references. You MUST include icons for: CloudFront, S3, API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB, and Amazon Bedrock. Reuse .tmp-ref/aws-icons/cloudfront.svg and .tmp-ref/aws-icons/s3.svg (same author/pattern). For API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB, and Bedrock, fetch the official AWS Architecture Icons from the same author's other public repos if present, or author clean small SVG icons consistent in style (48-64px viewBox, AWS service brand color background + white glyph). Network is OPEN_INTERNET; gh CLI is available. Document where each icon came from in findings.

Author docs/architecture.drawio as the editable source of truth: an <mxfile> draw.io document. Title it 'AI Monster — Architecture'. Lay out THIS architecture: (1) a 'User (Web Browser)' box labeled 'React + Vite SPA / EN·JA' on the left; (2) a dashed 'AWS Cloud (us-east-1)' boundary containing: Amazon CloudFront (note: HTTPS redirect, OAC), Amazon S3 (private, Block Public Access; holds frontend dist/ + config.json), API Gateway (HTTP API v2, CORS), FOUR Lambda functions clearly labeled getMonster / saveMonster / battle / chat, a DynamoDB table (DigitalMonsterStack-Monsters, PK=id), and Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic Claude). Use mxgraph.aws4.resourceIcon shapes for the AWS services. (3) Optionally a dashed note that infra is AWS CDK (TypeScript).

Wire the drawio edges to match reality: Browser --HTTPS--> CloudFront; CloudFront --OAC (SigV4), serves static--> S3 (private); Browser --reads config.json then calls API--> API Gateway; API Gateway --Lambda integration--> each of the 4 Lambdas (label the 4 routes: GET /monster/{monsterId}=getMonster, POST /monster=saveMonster, POST /battle=battle, POST /chat=chat); getMonster/saveMonster/battle --> DynamoDB; chat --> DynamoDB (read) AND chat --bedrock:InvokeModel--> Bedrock. CRITICAL: ONLY the chat Lambda connects to Bedrock (the other three have NO Bedrock edge). Add a small annotation noting baby stage returns a canned reply (no Bedrock) and rookie/champion/ultimate use Claude Haiku/Sonnet/Opus. Do NOT hardcode the live per-deploy CloudFront/API URLs into the diagram.

Author docs/architecture.svg by hand as a valid standalone SVG that depicts the SAME diagram as the drawio: white background, a title, the User box, the dashed 'AWS Cloud (us-east-1)' boundary, each AWS service drawn with its inlined official AWS icon path (reuse the icon <path> data from .tmp-ref/architecture.svg for CloudFront and S3; inline the glyphs for API Gateway, Lambda x4, DynamoDB, Bedrock from the docs/aws-icons assets), the 4 labeled Lambdas, DynamoDB, Bedrock, and arrows/labels matching the edges above (including the chat-only Bedrock edge). Make the viewBox/intrinsic width/height explicit (e.g. width/height attributes) so it rasterizes deterministically.

Generate docs/architecture.png by rasterizing docs/architecture.svg using the Playwright power's headless chromium (no host rasterizer exists). Approach: write a tiny HTML file that embeds the SVG at its intrinsic size (or open the SVG directly via a file:// URL), use browser_resize to the SVG's width/height, then browser_take_screenshot (type png) of the page/element. Screenshots are written under /projects/sandbox/.kiro/artifacts/screenshots/; move/copy the resulting PNG to docs/architecture.png. Verify the PNG is non-trivial (reasonable byte size, correct dimensions) and visually corresponds to the SVG. Document the exact tool/commands used in findings.
Delete the temporary .tmp-ref/ scratch directory (and ensure it is NOT committed). Confirm no application/infra source changed.
git add docs/ and commit on the docs/architecture-and-readme branch with a clear message, e.g. 'docs: add architecture diagram (drawio/svg/png) + aws-icons'.
acceptance_criteria: docs/architecture.drawio exists, is valid draw.io XML (opens as an <mxfile>/<mxGraphModel>), uses AWS service icons, and depicts: Browser -> CloudFront -> private S3 (OAC); Browser -> API Gateway (HTTP API) -> 4 named Lambdas (getMonster/saveMonster/battle/chat) -> DynamoDB; chat -> Bedrock, with ONLY chat connected to Bedrock.
docs/architecture.svg exists, is a valid standalone SVG with explicit width/height, and depicts the SAME diagram as the drawio (same services, same edges, chat-only Bedrock).
docs/architecture.png exists, is a valid PNG raster of the SVG with sensible dimensions matching the SVG aspect, and visually matches the SVG.
docs/aws-icons/ contains SVG icon assets for CloudFront, S3, API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB, and Bedrock that the diagram references.
The diagram does NOT hardcode per-deploy live CloudFront/API URLs.
No files under packages/ or infra/ were modified; .tmp-ref/ is not committed.
verification: git ls-files docs/ lists architecture.drawio, architecture.svg, architecture.png, and the docs/aws-icons/*.svg assets
python3 -c "import xml.dom.minidom,sys; xml.dom.minidom.parse('docs/architecture.drawio')" parses without error (well-formed XML)
file docs/architecture.png reports a PNG image with non-zero dimensions (or python: from struct import unpack; verify PNG signature + IHDR width/height > 0)
grep -c 'getMonster\|saveMonster\|battle\|chat' docs/architecture.drawio shows all four Lambda names present; confirm (by reading) exactly one Bedrock edge originates from the chat Lambda
git status confirms no packages/ or infra/ changes and no .tmp-ref/ tracked
findings:
Committed on branch docs/architecture-and-readme as cf4c947 'docs: add architecture diagram (drawio/svg/png) + aws-icons'. All three diagram files depict the SAME architecture, verified against infra/lib/digital-monster-stack.ts: Browser (React+Vite SPA, EN/JA) --HTTPS--> CloudFront (HTTPS redirect, OAC, SPA 403/404 fallback) --OAC(SigV4)--> private S3 (Block Public Access ALL, holds dist/+config.json); Browser --reads config.json then calls API--> API Gateway (HTTP API v2, CORS) --4 labeled routes--> 4 Lambdas: GET /monster/{monsterId}=getMonster (DynamoDB R/W), POST /monster=saveMonster (W), POST /battle=battle (R/W), POST /chat=chat (DynamoDB read). ONLY the chat Lambda has a single green bedrock:InvokeModel edge to Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic Claude); the other three Lambdas have NO Bedrock edge. A dashed note records the stage->model tier mapping (baby=canned reply/no Bedrock call, rookie=Claude Haiku, champion=Claude Sonnet, ultimate=Claude Opus) and a CDK/BucketDeployment note. No per-deploy live CloudFront/API URLs are hardcoded (grep for cloudfront.net/execute-api => 0 hits in both drawio and svg).

FILES: docs/architecture.drawio (editable <mxfile>, uses shape=mxgraph.aws4.resourceIcon with resIcon=cloudfront/s3/api_gateway/lambda/dynamodb/bedrock inside a dashed 'AWS Cloud (us-east-1)' boundary); docs/architecture.svg (hand-authored standalone SVG, explicit width=1180 height=720 viewBox 0 0 1180 720, inlines the official AWS architecture-icon <path> glyphs; the 4 Lambda icons share one <symbol id=lambda-icon> referenced via <use>); docs/architecture.png (1180x720, ~113 KB raster of the SVG).

AWS-ICON PROVENANCE (docs/aws-icons/): cloudfront.svg and s3.svg copied verbatim from the reference repo cache .tmp-ref/aws-icons/ (daichiasada/kiro-worldriskmap, same author/pattern). lambda.svg fetched via gh CLI from aws/aws-lambda-java-libs (experimental/aws-lambda-java-profiler/docs/Arch_AWS-Lambda_64.svg) - official AWS Architecture Icon with the orange C8511B->FF9900 gradient. api-gateway.svg, dynamodb.svg, bedrock.svg fetched via gh CLI from the official AWS Architecture-Service-Icons set vendored in error505/azure-cloud-ai-visualizer (Architecture-Service-Icons_07312025: Arch_Amazon-API-Gateway_64 #8C4FFF, Arch_Amazon-DynamoDB_64 #C925D1 under Arch_Database, Arch_Amazon-Bedrock_64 #01A88D). Each saved as a clean standalone 80x80 (S3 is 48x48) viewBox SVG with brand-color background + white glyph. All 6 parse as well-formed XML.

PNG RASTERIZATION (no host SVG->PNG tool exists; rsvg-convert/inkscape/convert/magick/dot/drawio/chromium and sharp/puppeteer all ABSENT). Used the Playwright power's headless chromium via the kiro_powers tool. IMPORTANT ENV FINDINGS: (1) file:// navigation is BLOCKED by the Playwright backend ('Access to file: protocol is blocked'); (2) a local python/node HTTP server is NOT reachable from the Playwright chromium and background servers do NOT survive across tool calls in this sandbox (they are reaped between calls - confirmed repeatedly), so serving over http://localhost failed with ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED; (3) browser_run_code_unsafe failed with 'TypeError: __fn__ is not a function' and could not be used; (4) data: URLs work but a single navigate argument carrying the full ~41KB (or minified ~28KB) data URI reliably interrupted the tool's input stream. WORKING APPROACH: navigate to a tiny blank data:text/html page, then build the SVG markup incrementally with repeated browser_evaluate calls - each call did window.__svg += atob('<base64 chunk>') with the SVG split into 7 small base64 chunks (<6KB each) to stay under the arg-size limit; a final browser_evaluate created an SVG element (document.createElementNS), set width/height/viewBox and innerHTML=window.__svg, and appended it to document.body. Then browser_resize to 1180x720 and browser_take_screenshot(type=png, scale=css, fullPage=false). The screenshot landed at /projects/sandbox/.kiro/artifacts/screenshots/page-2026-10-05T00-00-53-799Z.png; copied to docs/architecture.png. Verified: PNG signature + IHDR = 1180x720, 115761 bytes, and a visual read confirmed it matches the SVG/drawio (all 6 service icons, 4 named Lambdas, all labeled edges, and the single green chat->Bedrock edge). Note: for the raster path a visually identical minified SVG (path coords rounded to <=1 decimal, comments/whitespace stripped, Lambda icon deduped via <symbol>) was used to fit the arg-size limit; the committed docs/architecture.svg is the full hand-authored source. All scratch files (docs/_*.txt, _min.svg, _raster.html, _chunks/, _datauri*.txt, _scaffold.txt) and .tmp-ref/ were deleted before committing.

VERIFICATION: python3 xml.dom.minidom parses both docs/architecture.drawio and docs/architecture.svg without error; grep -c for the 4 Lambda names in the drawio = 15 (all four present); exactly one Bedrock edge (mxCell id=b1 source=lchat target=bedrock); git status shows no packages/ or infra/ changes and .tmp-ref not tracked. Sanity gate stayed green: npm run test => 47/47 pass; npm run build => shared/backend/frontend/infra all build OK (frontend dist/ is a gitignored build artifact and was NOT committed). Committed only the 9 docs/ files (3 diagrams + 6 icons).
